nary_nodes.label: War on Iran
evidence: Since the United States and Israel launched a war on Iran in late February, the global energy sector has undergone major upheaval.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; war is not a user interaction or sports event.

nary_nodes.label: US-Iran negotiations
evidence: But while ongoing US-Iran negotiations to reach a lasting peace have raised hopes for a return to stability in oil and gas markets, the war has already transformed the global energy landscape in ways that are likely to be long-lasting and even permanent, according to energy experts.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; negotiations are not sales or conferences.

nary_nodes.label: Signing of MoU
evidence: While Iran agreed to make its “best efforts” to arrange the safe passage of vessels in the strait in the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed with the US on June 17, Tehran has since then repeatedly claimed the right to control the critical waterway.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; signing is not a user interaction or performance.

nary_nodes.label: Attacks on commercial ships
evidence: After hitting a post-war peak of more than 70 transits on June 24, maritime traffic dropped sharply again over the weekend after attacks on two commercial ships that were widely blamed on Iran reignited fears for seafarers’ safety.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An act of aggression or violence against a target.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; attacks are not user interactions.

nary_nodes.label: Drop in maritime traffic
evidence: After hitting a post-war peak of more than 70 transits on June 24, maritime traffic dropped sharply again over the weekend after attacks on two commercial ships that were widely blamed on Iran reignited fears for seafarers’ safety.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A category of watercraft, such as commercial vessels.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; traffic changes are not user interactions or sales.

nary_nodes.label: Pipeline expansion
evidence: Facing ongoing threats in the waterway, energy suppliers have sought to ramp up exports on land via Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, the United Arab Emirates’ Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline, and the Iraq-Turkiye Crude Oil Pipeline – though the pipelines’ combined capacity falls well short of the approximately 20 million barrels of oil that moved through the strait each day before the war.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; expansion is not an education or children's event.

nary_nodes.label: Acceleration of renewables
evidence: Another anticipated legacy of the war is an acceleration in countries’ efforts to shift from fossil fuels to renewables, such as wind, solar and hydropower.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; transition is not a broadcast or delivery event.

nary_nodes.label: Record renewable capacity
evidence: Global renewable energy capacity hit a record high in 2025, with non-fossil fuel projects accounting for approximately 86 percent of added power capacity that year, according to the intergovernmental International Renewable Energy Agency.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; capacity increase is not a performance or broadcast.

evidence: “Following this war, few people looking for a new car will opt for one with an internal combustion engine,” Oxford University’s Imsirovic said.
nary_nodes.type_definition: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; market shift is not a sale or business event.

nary_nodes.label: Bring forward investments
evidence: “The conflict may ultimately bring forward investment decisions that were already in motion,” Elheddad told Al Jazeera.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of expanding infrastructure, such as a pipeline expansion.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class fits; investment decision is not an education or business event.

nary_nodes.label: Oil market never same
evidence: “The oil market will never be the same, following this conflict,” Adi Imsirovic, a veteran oil trader who lectures at the University of Oxford, told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: New pipelines and security
evidence: “New pipelines will urgently be built. New security arrangements will be put into place, and the buyers of oil from the region will look elsewhere for diversification,” Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Long-term concern over transits
evidence: Dan Marks, a research fellow in energy security at the Royal United Services Institute in London, said he expects there to be “long-term” concern over transits in the strait.

nary_nodes.label: Possibility of strait closure
evidence: ‘“While the current Iranian regime remains in place and at odds with the United States and Israel, there will always be the possibility that tensions will flare and the strait will close,” Marks told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: Reduced reliance on strait
evidence: June Goh, a Singapore-based senior oil market analyst at Sparta, a commodities data firm, said she anticipates a sustained push by energy producers and consumers alike to reduce their reliance on the strait.

nary_nodes.label: More pipeline routes
evidence: “For the producers, this would come in the form of more pipeline evacuation routes from the Middle East,” Goh told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: Maintain strategic reserves
evidence: “For the buyers, this would mean maintaining a healthy supply of strategic petroleum reserves.”

“For the buyers, this would mean maintaining a healthy supply of strategic petroleum reserves.” June Goh, a Singapore-based senior oil market analyst at Sparta, a commodities data firm, said she anticipates a sustained push by energy producers and consumers alike to reduce their reliance on the strait.

nary_nodes.label: War supercharging renewables
evidence: In April, Simon Stiell, the top United Nations climate official, told a meeting of government officials at the International Energy Agency that the conflict was already “supercharging the global renewables boom”.

nary_nodes.label: EV preference post-war
evidence: “Following this war, few people looking for a new car will opt for one with an internal combustion engine,” Oxford University’s Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: End of oil monopoly
evidence: “And this will finish the important monopoly of oil in road transportation,” Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Strengthen renewables case
evidence: While energy security imperatives are likely to lead many governments to stockpile fossil fuels in the near-term, the medium to long-term economic case for renewables will strengthen as geopolitical risk inflates “the true cost” of fossil fuel dependence, said Mohamed Elheddad, an associate lecturer in economics at the University of Lancashire in the United Kingdom.

nary_nodes.label: China benefits
evidence: “China will benefit, given its dominance in providing renewable energy infrastructure products,” Obstfeld told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: US and Qatar consolidate
evidence: “The US strengthens its position as a swing LNG supplier. Qatar consolidates its role as a reliable long-term contract partner.”

“The US strengthens its position as a swing LNG supplier. Qatar consolidates its role as a reliable long-term contract partner.” Other countries such as the US and Qatar may also be able to consolidate their positions as leading energy suppliers in the aftermath of the war, said Elheddad, the University of Lancashire lecturer.
